title: Triple-dominance pair counting
code:
from bisect import bisect_right

def count_dominant_pairs(seq: list[int]) -> int:
    values = sorted(set(seq))
    m = len(values)
    pos = {v: i + 1 for i, v in enumerate(values)}
    bit = [0] * (m + 1)

    total = 0
    seen = 0
    bisect_right_local = bisect_right
    bit_local = bit
    pos_local = pos

    for x in seq:
        k = bisect_right_local(values, 3 * x)

        le = 0
        j = k
        while j:
            le += bit_local[j]
            j -= j & -j

        total += seen - le
        seen += 1

        i = pos_local[x]
        while i <= m:
            bit_local[i] += 1
            i += i & -i

    return total

title: Smallest solution of congruences with non-coprime moduli
code:
import math


def solve_congruences(pairs):
    x = 0
    mod = 1

    for r, m in pairs:
        a = r % m
        g = math.gcd(mod, m)
        diff = a - x

        if diff % g != 0:
            raise ValueError("inconsistent congruences")

        mod_g = mod // g
        m_g = m // g
        lcm = mod_g * m

        if m_g == 1:
            t = 0
        else:
            inv = pow(mod_g % m_g, -1, m_g)
            t = ((diff // g) % m_g) * inv % m_g

        x = (x + mod * t) % lcm
        mod = lcm

    return x

title: Parity-locked divisible pairs
code:
def count_locked_pairs(values: list[int], m: int) -> int:
    if m < 1:
        raise ValueError("m must be >= 1")

    # If m is even, a sum that is a multiple of m is automatically even,
    # so the parity condition is redundant. If m is odd, "same parity" is
    # equivalent to the sum being even, i.e. a multiple of lcm(m, 2) = 2m.
    # Either way, the problem reduces to counting pairs with
    # (values[i] + values[j]) % M == 0, where M is always even.
    M = m if (m & 1) == 0 else 2 * m

    counts = [0] * M
    for v in values:
        counts[v % M] += 1

    half = M // 2
    total = 0

    # Complementary residue pairs (r, M - r) with 1 <= r < M - r.
    for r in range(1, half):
        total += counts[r] * counts[M - r]

    # Self-complementary residues: 0 and M // 2.
    c = counts[0]
    total += c * (c - 1) // 2
    c = counts[half]
    total += c * (c - 1) // 2

    return total

title: Mergeable component ledger with undo
code:
class MergeLedger:
    """Labeled elements partitioned into components with mergeable,
    undoable unions and per-component size/value aggregates.

    Implemented as a rollback union-find: union-by-size without path
    compression keeps tree depth O(log n), and every value change is
    propagated to all ancestors so that each node always stores the
    current aggregate of its own subtree. A merge can then be reversed
    by detaching the recorded child root and subtracting its (current)
    subtree aggregates from the parent root.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self._parent = {}    # label -> parent label (roots map to themselves)
        self._size = {}      # label -> size of its union-tree subtree
        self._sum = {}       # label -> value sum of its union-tree subtree
        self._count = 0      # number of components
        self._history = []   # stack of (child_root, parent_root) per successful merge

    def _require(self, x):
        if x not in self._parent:
            raise KeyError(x)

    def _find(self, x):
        parent = self._parent
        while parent[x] != x:
            x = parent[x]
        return x

    def add(self, x, value=0):
        if x in self._parent:
            raise ValueError(f"element already exists: {x!r}")
        self._parent[x] = x
        self._size[x] = 1
        self._sum[x] = value
        self._count += 1

    def merge(self, a, b):
        self._require(a)
        self._require(b)
        ra = self._find(a)
        rb = self._find(b)
        if ra == rb:
            return False
        if self._size[ra] < self._size[rb]:
            ra, rb = rb, ra
        self._parent[rb] = ra
        self._size[ra] += self._size[rb]
        self._sum[ra] += self._sum[rb]
        self._history.append((rb, ra))
        self._count -= 1
        return True

    def same(self, a, b):
        self._require(a)
        self._require(b)
        return self._find(a) == self._find(b)

    def component_size(self, x):
        self._require(x)
        return self._size[self._find(x)]

    def component_value(self, x):
        self._require(x)
        return self._sum[self._find(x)]

    def add_value(self, x, delta):
        self._require(x)
        parent = self._parent
        while True:
            self._sum[x] += delta
            if parent[x] == x:
                break
            x = parent[x]

    def components(self):
        return self._count

    def undo(self):
        if not self._history:
            raise RuntimeError("no merge to undo")
        child, parent = self._history.pop()
        self._parent[child] = child
        self._size[parent] -= self._size[child]
        self._sum[parent] -= self._sum[child]
        self._count += 1

title: Longest echoed slice
code:
def longest_echo(s: str) -> int:
    n = len(s)
    if n < 2:
        return 0

    # Suffix automaton: the longest repeated substring is the maximum
    # length[v] over states whose endpos set has size >= 2.
    trans = [{}]
    link = [-1]
    length = [0]
    occ = [0]
    last = 0

    for c in s.encode():  # c is the byte value of each lowercase letter
        cur = len(length)
        length.append(length[last] + 1)
        link.append(0)
        occ.append(1)
        trans.append({})
        p = last
        while p != -1:
            d = trans[p]
            if c in d:
                q = d[c]
                break
            d[c] = cur
            p = link[p]
        else:  # fell off the root
            link[cur] = 0
            last = cur
            continue
        if length[p] + 1 == length[q]:
            link[cur] = q
        else:
            clone = len(length)
            length.append(length[p] + 1)
            link.append(link[q])
            occ.append(0)
            trans.append(trans[q].copy())
            while p != -1 and trans[p].get(c) == q:
                trans[p][c] = clone
                p = link[p]
            link[q] = clone
            link[cur] = clone
        last = cur

    # Order states by length via counting sort.
    size = len(length)
    cnt = [0] * (n + 1)
    for l in length:
        cnt[l] += 1
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        cnt[i] += cnt[i - 1]
    order = [0] * size
    for i in range(size - 1, -1, -1):
        l = length[i]
        cnt[l] -= 1
        order[cnt[l]] = i

    # Propagate occurrence counts from longest to shortest states.
    # The first state (longest) with occ >= 2 gives the answer.
    for i in range(size - 1, 0, -1):
        v = order[i]
        if occ[v] >= 2:
            return length[v]
        p = link[v]
        if p != -1:
            occ[p] += occ[v]
    return 0

title: Largest-remainder integer allocation
code:
from fractions import Fraction


def allocate_shares(total: int, weights: list) -> list[int]:
    if total < 0:
        raise ValueError("total must be >= 0")
    if not weights:
        raise ValueError("weights must be a non-empty list")
    if any(w < 0 for w in weights):
        raise ValueError("all weights must be >= 0")

    fw = [Fraction(w) for w in weights]
    W = sum(fw)
    if W <= 0:
        raise ValueError("sum of weights must be > 0")

    quotas = [Fraction(total) * w / W for w in fw]
    floors = [q.numerator // q.denominator for q in quotas]
    remainders = [q - f for q, f in zip(quotas, floors)]

    shares = list(floors)
    leftover = total - sum(floors)

    order = sorted(range(len(weights)), key=lambda i: (-remainders[i], i))
    for i in order[:leftover]:
        shares[i] += 1

    return shares

title: Interval scheduling with mandatory cooldown gap
code:
def max_sessions(intervals, gap):
    """
    Return the maximum number of sessions that can be scheduled in one room
    such that consecutive selected sessions satisfy
    next_start >= previous_end + gap.

    Greedy earliest-finish-time selection (optimal for interval scheduling):
    sorting by end time and always taking the first compatible session leaves
    the room free as early as possible, which never reduces the number of
    sessions that can still follow. Runs in O(n log n).
    """
    count = 0
    last_end = None
    for start, end in sorted(intervals, key=lambda iv: iv[1]):
        if last_end is None or start >= last_end + gap:
            count += 1
            last_end = end
    return count

def chunk_evenly(items, n: int) -> list[list]:
    if n < 1:
        raise ValueError("n must be at least 1")
    data = list(items)
    total = len(data)
    base, extra = divmod(total, n)
    chunks = []
    start = 0
    for i in range(n):
        size = base + 1 if i < extra else base
        chunks.append(data[start:start + size])
        start += size
    return chunks

title: Divisible pulse windows with bounded length
code:
def count_pulses(deltas: list[int], k: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    n = len(deltas)
    if not (1 <= lo <= hi <= n):
        raise ValueError("require 1 <= lo <= hi <= len(deltas)")

    # Prefix sums reduced modulo k: subarray (i, j] sums to a multiple of k
    # iff pref[i] == pref[j].
    pref = [0] * (n + 1)
    s = 0
    for i, v in enumerate(deltas, 1):
        s = (s + v) % k
        pref[i] = s

    counts = {}
    get = counts.get
    total = 0

    # For each end j, valid starts i satisfy j - hi <= i <= j - lo.
    # Slide that window of start residues across the prefix array.
    for j in range(lo, n + 1):
        r = pref[j - lo]               # newest start index enters the window
        counts[r] = get(r, 0) + 1
        if j > hi:                     # oldest start index leaves the window
            r_old = pref[j - hi - 1]
            c = counts[r_old] - 1
            if c:
                counts[r_old] = c
            else:
                del counts[r_old]
        total += get(pref[j], 0)

    return total

title: Cheapest walk with color-switch surcharge
code:
import heapq


def min_cost_route(n, edges, s, t, switch_cost):
    if s == t:
        return 0

    # Expanded graph:
    #   - node ids 0 .. n-1 are "plain" vertices (used as switch hubs)
    #   - one state node (v, color) for each color of an edge incident to v
    # Edges:
    #   - (v, c) -> v with weight switch_cost   (pay to switch away from color c)
    #   - v -> (v, c) with weight 0             (adopt color c for free)
    #   - (u, c) <-> (v, c) with weight w for each original edge (u, v, w, c)
    # Starting at plain vertex s makes the first edge free of switch charge.
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    states_at = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    state_id = {}

    def get_state(v, c):
        key = (v, c)
        idx = state_id.get(key)
        if idx is None:
            idx = len(adj)
            state_id[key] = idx
            adj.append([(v, switch_cost)])
            adj[v].append((idx, 0))
            states_at[v].append(idx)
        return idx

    for u, v, w, c in edges:
        iu = get_state(u, c)
        iv = get_state(v, c)
        adj[iu].append((iv, w))
        adj[iv].append((iu, w))

    INF = float('inf')
    dist = [INF] * len(adj)
    dist[s] = 0
    pq = [(0, s)]
    push = heapq.heappush
    pop = heapq.heappop
    while pq:
        d, x = pop(pq)
        if d != dist[x]:
            continue
        for y, w in adj[x]:
            nd = d + w
            if nd < dist[y]:
                dist[y] = nd
                push(pq, (nd, y))

    ans = INF
    for idx in states_at[t]:
        if dist[idx] < ans:
            ans = dist[idx]
    return -1 if ans == INF else ans
